Thanks for the heads up. Quick notes and next steps: 

- Documentation: we need either the occupational health (OH) fit note or a surgeon's note that lists activity restrictions. Emma's discharge/recovery plan is helpful but not sufficient for our records.
- Checklist & forms: attaching our RTW_checklist_v3.pdf and the ergonomic_assessment_form.pdf — please have Emma fill the assessment where possible before the onsite check.
- Contractor accommodations: we treat contractor RTW requests the same as employees for safety/operational reasons; we can offer temporary flexible schedule, hybrid remote allowance, and reasonable workstation modifications. No paid leave obligations apply, but we will work with the manager on schedule and short-term coverage.
- Occupational health: I recommend a brief OH assessment to document restrictions. I've tentatively reached out to Oakridge (occhealth@oakridgeclinic.com) for a tele-assessment the morning of 3/10 and asked for a formal note.

Can we plan a short three-point phased schedule draft and get Emma's availability for the 3/10 OH slot? Stephanie/Laura — if Emma returns 3/16 with limited commuting, we should line up key deliverables and a coverage plan for any days she is remote.
